spec.title: The Sweep Playbook — the standing guardian

p.fact: **Discipline v0.2 · status: BETA · T1 · language-neutral**
*The recurring counterpart of the [Raid Playbook](03-RAID-PLAYBOOK.md).*
*A raid is a scheduled campaign — scoped, planned, finite.*
*The **sweep** is the standing run that, executed daily (or several times a day on an active tree), keeps a codebase inside the Discipline instead of letting it drift back out between campaigns.*
*Terraforming brings a tree into the Discipline ([BROWNFIELD](mechanisms/BROWNFIELD-PROTOCOL-v0.1.md)); raids move it in planned steps; the sweep holds the ground in between.*

*Each language stack ships the concrete tools and idioms (the Rust stack: `rust-ai-native floor | health | test-gate | tripwire`, plus the sweep-idiom section of its GUIDE); this document is the method.*

item.fact: **The gates are the floor; the sweep is the ceiling.** The binary gates — format check, tests, lints, the conform gate, the specmap check — say pass/fail and MUST be green before any sweep work. The collector's advisory facts (coverage gaps, danger bands, backlogs) sit *above* that floor and say what to harden next. A green sweep on a red floor is a contradiction: fix the floor.
**The gate is truth; the collector is a guide.** When the collector says a unit is ready to gate, the gate confirms or refutes it. Trust the gate.

p.fact: Law 2 governs the sweep's shape: explanation capital must be runnable capital, so the sweep is **collector-first** — a deterministic, no-LLM fact-gatherer (the stack's `health` tool) computes the objective state, and the operator (human or agent) acts on facts, not vibes.
Where a check cannot be mechanised yet (the WISH rules), the sweep names it and routes it to judgment — it never pretends prose is a gate.
**Tier 0 — the hard floor (every run, binary, first).** Never sweep on a red tree.
Run the stack's floor command (format → build/tests → lints → conform gate → traceability check → test-gate where a baseline registry exists → fast-loop budgets where enforced).
If any gate is red, the only work is making it green.
**Tier 1 — the ratchet (every run; act on the collector's facts).** Run the health collector and work its output in cheapest-win-first order.
The canonical moves, each driven by a collector field, never by memory:

item.fact: **Split the danger band before it trips** — files approaching the length budget are landmines; measure with the rule (physical lines), not the eye.
**Widen a gate for free** — a unit the collector shows at zero drain (e.g. full doctest coverage) enters the corresponding gate list with zero work; the gate run confirms the prediction.

**Drain the smallest backlog** — take the smallest-gap ungated unit, bring it to zero, then flip it into the gate (the expand-as-you-conform rhythm: **a unit enters a gate only after it drains to zero** — a flip must never widen a baseline).

**Re-justify the deviation debt** — walk each recorded deviation: does its reason still hold? A deviation whose invariant has since been encoded in a type/checker is removed and restructured. *A deviation with no live reason is a defect.*

**Catch census regressions** — for gated units the violation censuses must stay zero; a non-zero is a fresh violation that slipped a local check. Restructure beats testify: encode the invariant in a type or contract rather than recording an excuse.

p.fact: **Tier 2 — drift (weekly; the slow rot the gates don't see).**

item.fact: **Debt registry:** run the tripwire tool; re-disposition any touched-and-open entry ([BROWNFIELD §3](mechanisms/BROWNFIELD-PROTOCOL-v0.1.md#registries)). New deficiencies found while sweeping are *filed* there, not left as prose.

**Doc/code drift:** state checkpoints vs reality (see [WAL convention](06-WAL-CONVENTION.md) — freshness rule); architecture docs vs the real layout; roadmap self-staleness. A stale doc that governs code is filed as `stale-doc` debt.

**Marker census:** every TODO/FIXME/REVIEW/HACK is a WISH or a deferred decision — load-bearing ones graduate into the debt/intent registries, trivial ones are resolved or deleted. Prose that promises and doesn't deliver is false training signal.
**Golden transcripts:** characterization oracles must fail loudly and be re-captured deliberately, never auto-updated — an auto-updated golden is a test that always passes.
**Traceability kind hygiene:** a code edge into an unmarked spec unit prompts marking the unit's kind/revision in the same change — a unit that code points at is not informative.

p.fact: **Tier 3 — deep judgment (weekly/biweekly; the WISH rules).** The rules no checker mechanises yet — reviewed by a human or strong agent so they are not silently skipped, each a candidate to graduate into a real checker.
The stack's GUIDE and cards carry the concrete list (typed seams, cell isolation and oracles, uniformity, contract-first ordering, lying prose, closed-vocabulary naming).
Tier 3 may also launch a full [raid](03-RAID-PLAYBOOK.md) when a Tier-1 backlog grows campaign-sized — plan it per the [Campaign Form](05-CAMPAIGN-FORM.md).
The health collector is the sweep's instrument.
It MUST be:

item.fact: **deterministic** (same tree → byte-identical output, so its committed snapshot's diff IS the health trend),
**advisory** (it never fails the build — the gates do),
**no-LLM**,
and **single-sourced** (it reads the gate policies — the conform and specmap configs — never hardcoded lists, so its numbers cannot drift from what the gates enforce).

p.fact: Count the list, not the record: any inventory the sweep acts on comes from the collector or a config, never from memory or a document's stale snapshot.
**The promotion ladder** — how the rule set grows: a Tier-3 WISH rule becomes mechanisable → add it to the collector as a census (cheap, advisory) → once proven, promote it to a blocking gate rule.
Extending the collector is itself ratchet work.
The daily run is light: floor green, then one or two cheapest Tier-1 wins.
The weekly run adds the drift and judgment tiers.
**Any single item is a safe stop** — the sweep is incremental by construction, and the collector re-derives the remaining work each run.
Each sweep that changes the tree lands topic-grouped commits (one logical unit each), citing the sweep item that drove them.
Refresh the committed health snapshot in the same run — its diff records the trend.
**Resume pointer** (see [06-WAL-CONVENTION](06-WAL-CONVENTION.md)):

item.fact: *With a WAL (recommended):* bump the WAL's standing line at any sweep that moves a milestone (a gate widened, a backlog unit cleared); the health snapshot plus the WAL is the next sweep's starting point.

*Without a WAL:* the sweep's closing commit message carries the summary — floor state, the Tier-1 items taken, the next candidate — and the committed health snapshot is the resume pointer. Nothing may live only in the operator's head or the session transcript.

section.title: 5. What the sweep deliberately does NOT do

item.fact: It does **not** replace the gates (Tier 0 is the floor, the sweep hardens what sits above it).
It does **not** auto-fix. The collector gathers facts; the operator acts. Mechanising a fix is a separate, deliberate promotion (a new gate rule or a codemod).
It does **not** touch owner-frozen surfaces or owner-court decisions without sanction; drift found in them is *filed* as debt, not fixed.
It does **not** measure effectiveness (deferred by design); it records objective state.

p.fact: A consumer project runs the sweep from the shipped skill (the Rust stack ships `rust-ai-native-sweep`) against the shipped tools; the only per-project material is the policy files the gates already require and, optionally, a thin local instance document recording project snapshot numbers and machine-scoped quirks.
Keep the three layers apart: **method** (this document), **language idioms** (the stack's GUIDE/cards), **project instance** (the consumer's own notes).
A machine quirk is not project fact; a project number is not method.
